summary: 15 concise trial-paper-only hypotheses distilled from the ResearchAgent run for accord, grouped by per-hypothesis feature attribution.

mechanisms.description: In ACCORD‑BP participants with high baseline CSVD (WMH/ICV ≥75th percentile or presence of lacunes/microbleeds), randomized intensive SBP target (<120 mmHg) will cause greater absolute annual decline in the harmonized global cognitive z‑score than standard treatment due to reduced cerebral perfusion reserve and resultant hypoperfusion.

Elevated baseline carotid–femoral PWV (≥10 m/s) will amplify the adverse effect of intensive versus standard BP lowering on cognitive slope by limiting vascular compliance and impairing cerebral autoregulatory capacity.

Participants with combined high CSVD and elevated PWV randomized to intensive BP control will experience higher absolute rates of adjudicated falls and orthostatic syncope than low‑vulnerability participants because impaired cerebrovascular reserve increases susceptibility to hypotension‑related symptomatic events.

High baseline WMH burden will modify the intensive‑treatment effect by increasing absolute risk of incident stroke even if macrovascular MACE reductions persist in other strata, reflecting regional vulnerability to lowered perfusion under intensive lowering.

Presence of lacunes or microbleeds at baseline will interact with intensive BP lowering to produce a larger absolute increase in cognitive decline than in participants without those lesions, independent of baseline covariates.

Baseline arterial stiffness measured by PWV will modify the effect of intensive treatment on MACE such that macrovascular benefits are attenuated in the high‑PWV stratum because cerebral/functional harms offset some large‑vessel gains.

Intensive BP lowering will disproportionately increase all‑cause mortality in the high‑CSVD stratum through cumulative cerebral and functional insults (accelerated cognitive decline, falls, stroke) relative to low‑CSVD participants.

The excess cognitive decline observed with intensive treatment among participants with high WMH/ICV will be mediated in part by an increased frequency of documented hypotensive or orthostatic episodes during follow‑up.

Greater baseline PWV will interact with intensive BP lowering to exacerbate the deleterious effects of BP variability on cognition, producing the largest absolute cognitive slope declines in participants with both high PWV and high on‑treatment BP variability.

Intensive systolic BP reduction will produce larger absolute harms on cognitive trajectory in participants whose prespecified CSVD categorical score is high versus medium or low, even after adjustment for baseline cognitive score and comorbidities.

Participants with medium CSVD (WMH/ICV 25–75th percentile with ≤1 lacune/≤1 microbleed) will exhibit intermediate modification of intensive treatment effects on cognition and stroke risk, consistent with a graded dose–response across CSVD categories.

In participants meeting the elevated‑PWV threshold, intensive BP lowering will yield a less favorable net clinical balance, with greater NNH for clinically meaningful cognitive deterioration and falls relative to NNT for MACE reduction, compared with low‑PWV participants.

Modeling the interaction between treatment arm and continuous WMH/ICV with restricted cubic splines will reveal nonlinearity, with the steepest absolute cognitive harms under intensive treatment occurring above the top WMH quartile.

Adjustment for achieved on‑treatment SBP and BP variability will attenuate but not fully eliminate the treatment × modifier interaction, indicating partial mediation by attained BP and residual effect modification by pre‑existing brain vascular vulnerability.

Selection into the imaging/PWV substudy will not fully explain observed treatment‑modifier interactions, such that inverse‑probability weighted analyses will continue to show greater absolute cognitive and cerebral/functional harms from intensive BP lowering in high‑vulnerability participants.
